section_insight: The coach subsystem and API layer dominate churn. Three files stand out on relative churn: `streamlit/whoop/db.py` (relative churn 11.9x — 462 deletions against only 60 remaining lines, driven by iterative schema expansion across 7 commits over 18 days), `apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts` (7.1x, 18 commits over 12 days — a mix of feature additions, bug fixes, and a mid-stream refactor that split the file), and `apps/web/src/components/coach/CoachWorkspace.tsx` (6.4x, churned in a 1-day burst then decomposed). The chat route's commit history shows sustained churn from five distinct causes: agentic loop feature additions (streaming, tool_progress, JSON mode), repeated bug fixes on failure handling and SSE keepalive, a mid-project refactor (split into handler + loop + persistence), a caching iteration (three successive debug/fix commits to get prompt caching headers right), and then OAuth plumbing added on top. That layering pattern — features piled onto a file before its shape was stable — explains why relative churn is 7x. The sync boundary (`apps/web/src/app/api/sync/route.ts`, relative churn 2.65x; `apps/web/src/lib/whoop/upsert.ts`, 1.91x; `apps/web/src/app/api/whoop/webhook/route.ts`, 3.1x) shows a secondary concentration: the Whoop data pipeline was designed and then repeatedly corrected — cooldown logic, abort-after-commit semantics, transaction wrapping, DLQ addition — all within two weeks. Auth (`apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts`, 1.41x, 12 commits over 13 days) has the most sustained churn: it changed in 12 separate sessions across the full observation window, touching CF Access, Apple Sign In, sessions schema, OAuth state, and Cloudflare teardown. No single commit was a bug fix in isolation; auth kept changing because the identity model itself changed. Concentration: the top 10 files by commit count (chat route, coach loop, auth, sync route, db/connection, db/index, coach/tools, whoop/upsert, coach/prompts, db/sleep) account for ~60% of all commits in the tracked set. The coach subsystem alone (chat route + loop + prompts + tools + CoachWorkspace) represents the single highest-risk area — it is actively being extended, has the most bug-fix commits, and its core loop file has never had a stable period.
